item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The test log shows these little guys in an extremely artificial environment. Constrained space, first ample food then no food at all, no predators or competition, access to ample amounts of only specific materials, etc. Basically, a series of advantages and challenges that could have been tailor-made to encourage unfettered technological development.

In the wild, I could see a colony building up to pre-industrial then plateauing because there is no D-class coming in periodically to kick over the kilns, thus no motivation to develop defenses.

Or the tech curve of a Texas desert colony going off on a wild tangent because there is nothing but rocks and sand to work with, but there are armadillos to worry about. Inevitably culminating in termite Paul Atreides riding the "great armored sand monster" to prove his worthiness to lead the hive.

What I'm saying is that what we are shown is probably the single most dangerous scenario possible. The fact that uncontained colonies haven't taken over the Earth yet would tend to support that hypothesis; and the Euclid rating.

Okay, so, I believe it would be likely that the Foundation would be very strict about ensuring no cross contamination between SCP-831 and SCP-1006, since imagine how much harder it would be to contain SCP-831 if it had a political agenda on top of its usual abilities. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

Colonies of SCP-831 encountered outside of Foundation containment are to be immediately eradicated. Individual organisms of SCP-831 can easily be exterminated by fire, crushing, asphyxiation or many other methods. However, sufficiently advanced colonies of SCP-831 can be expected to have constructed defense mechanisms. After eradication, objects found in colony’s location are to be brought to Site-36 or Site-181 for analysis.

To this:

Colonies of SCP-831 encountered outside of Foundation containment are to be immediately eradicated. Individual organisms of SCP-831 can easily be exterminated by fire, crushing, asphyxiation or many other methods. However, sufficiently advanced colonies of SCP-831 can be expected to have constructed defense mechanisms. After eradication, objects found in colony’s location are to be brought to Site-36 or Site-181 for analysis.

Due to the potential dangers of cross contamination at no point may colonies of SCP-831 be allowed contact with SCP-1006.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
Realize this is a massive necropost, but I find this interesting so I thought I'd share: Basically FMOC-D-Alanine isn't useful in and of itself, but FMOC is what you call a protector group- you can take that and LEGO other chemicals onto it fairly easily, and then use that to make all sorts of interesting organic compounds. With the chemicals they had, you could:

  1. do extremely advanced biochemistry involving artificial peptide synthesis, such as creating macromolecules like complex polymers and Macromolecular assemblies (aka Nanotechnology)
  2. blow a lot of stuff up REAL good - Tetrazole is a component of solid rocket fuel and high explosives, for instance.

So if you wanted to, say, build an semi-organic spacecraft and blast your way out of a containment chamber, that'd be a pretty good place to start.
